title: Nothing to phish on a smart card

beats.say: Penny taps her smart card and she's logged in. Nothing typed.
Certificate-based authentication: you prove who you are with a certificate.
The private key stays in hardware, and there's no typed secret to steal.
So it counts as phishing-resistant MFA. Bolt asks for her password. Nothing to give.

facts.claim: Certificate-based authentication lets an org authenticate individual users with digital certificates.
facts.evidence: authenticate individual users with digital certificates

facts.claim: With certificate-based authentication there is no typed secret and the key stays in hardware.
facts.evidence: Because there is no typed secret and the key stays in hardware

facts.claim: Salesforce counts certificate-based authentication among the phishing-resistant forms of MFA.
facts.evidence: Salesforce counts this among the phishing-resistant forms of MFA
